# Product foundation

## Product
Chaser sends polite payment reminders for freelance designers, so they stop chasing late invoices by hand.

## Problem
Late invoices hurt, and designers hate asking for money. Today they keep a spreadsheet and write awkward emails weeks after the due date, or let it slide. This costs a few hours a month.

## Persona
A freelance brand or web designer who works alone, with 3 to 10 active clients. They invoice from a tool like Wave or from a PDF. They want to get paid on time without asking for money themselves. What stops them: they hate the ask, so they put it off or skip it.

## Not for
Agencies with a finance person.

Open: other sign-ups we should turn away (non-designers, freelancers outside design, designers with more than 10 clients).

## Goals
1. 50 paying users by the end of March 2027.
2. Grow fast after that. Open: no number or date after March 2027.

## Anti-goals
1. We will not build invoicing itself. Open: why (not stated).
2. No mobile app. Open: why (not stated).

## Assumptions
1. Designers will let a tool email their clients in their name. Not yet proven.

Open: price, since "paying users" has no price or plan.
Open: how reminders reach clients beyond email, if at all.
Open: how Chaser learns of an invoice (import from Wave, PDF upload, or manual entry).

questions.question: Should a designer with more than 10 clients, or a small studio of two or three people, be turned away or welcomed?
questions.why: The Persona says 3 to 10 clients and works alone, but Not for names only agencies with a finance person, so two readers will disagree on who a 15-client solo or a two-person studio is.
options: Turn away both; Persona is a hard line
Welcome more than 10 clients, turn away studios
Welcome both; 3 to 10 only describes the typical user
Welcome up to 3 people, any client count

questions.question: Do we turn away freelancers outside design (developers, writers, consultants) who sign up, or take their money and not market to them?
questions.why: With a goal of 50 paying users by March 2027, refusing paying sign-ups has a cost, and the answer decides whether Not for is a gate or only a marketing focus.
options: Turn them away at sign-up
Accept them, but do not market to them
Accept them and name them as a later persona
Undecided until we see who signs up

questions.question: Is a Wave or PDF invoicer the only designer we serve, or do designers who invoice from other tools (Stripe, QuickBooks, FreshBooks, Notion) count too?
questions.why: The Persona names only Wave and PDF, and the answer sets whether Chaser can learn of invoices at all for the people we say it is for.
options: Wave and PDF only
Add Stripe and QuickBooks
Any tool; Chaser takes manual entry too
Wave only at launch, others later

questions.question: Goal 2 ("Grow fast after that") has no number or date, so what should it say?
questions.why: As written it cannot be checked on any date, and it may pull toward the agencies and heavy-client designers the Not for section turns away.
options: 200 paying users by end of September 2027
$5,000 monthly revenue by end of December 2027
Drop it until goal 1 is met
Keep it, but name the number and date later

questions.question: What counts as a "paying user" in goal 1?
questions.why: With no price or plan, a $1 plan and a $50 plan both hit 50, so the goal can be met without a business behind it.
options: Any user on a paid plan, any price
A user paying at least a stated monthly price (name it)
A paying user who had a reminder sent in the last 30 days
Count monthly revenue instead of users

questions.question: Should a goal measure whether Chaser fixes the problem, such as late invoices getting paid?
questions.why: Both goals count customers, not outcomes, so 50 people could pay and the product could still not stop designers chasing invoices by hand.
options: Yes: most reminded invoices paid within 7 days of the first reminder
Yes: users report saving 2 or more hours a month
No: paying users is enough for now

questions.question: Will Chaser ever take the payment itself (a pay-now button, card or bank collection), or only prompt the client to pay through the designer's own invoice link?
questions.why: A team that chases late invoices will be tempted to add a pay button, and that turns a reminder tool into a payments product with its own regulation, fees and support load.
options: Never take payment; link to the designer's own invoice only
Allow a pay link to the designer's existing processor, no money through Chaser
Collect payment later, not in the first release
Collect payment from the start

questions.question: If a client ignores every polite reminder, does Chaser stop, or may it escalate to firm notices, late fees or a collections hand-off?
questions.why: Escalation is the obvious next feature for a tool that fails to get anyone paid, and it contradicts the polite, no-awkwardness promise in Product and Persona.
options: Never escalate; the tone stays polite and it stops after a set number of reminders
Escalate to one firm final notice, still sent in the designer's name
Add late fees and collections hand-off later
Escalate fully from the start

questions.question: Will Chaser build two-way sync with accounting and invoicing tools (Wave, QuickBooks, FreshBooks), or only read invoices in?
questions.why: Sync is the tempting route to 'learning of an invoice', but writing back to those tools drifts into the invoicing anti-goal and is a large maintenance cost for a one-person team.
options: Read-only import from Wave; no write-back, no other tools
Manual entry and PDF upload only, no integrations
Full two-way sync with several tools
Decide after the first 50 users
